name: cfcmt-bus-fit-action-ranking-v1
row_selection: All original target fit rows only; do not read stop/calibrate state rows or evaluation trajectories.
execution: Current canonical execution projection; all actor deterministic and stochastic component queries clipped. Recorded labels checked unchanged. Identical actions excluded from ranking preference denominators.
groups: All rows, free execution interval, forced60s interval; other collapsed intervals only if present. Compare unchanged states across all actors and critics.
critic_reduction: min-all over two heads separately for each sampled action, then Monte Carlo average; never min of head means.
actor_objective: J=-E[min Q]+alpha_stage E[latent log pi]. Gate weighted analytically, positive branch uses eight fixed common Normal draws. Same critic-stage alpha for all candidate actors within a row; diagonal reflects own checkpoint. Initial adapted actor was IQL, so its entry evaluates the prospective SAC objective rather than its original IQL loss.
gate_partial_derivative: At fixed positive distribution: Q component=-p(1-p)(E Qplus-Qzero); entropy component=alpha_stage*p(1-p)(logodds+E log fpositive). Negative loss derivative encourages larger gate probability. This is not a full shared-network optimizer step.
comparisons: Deterministic Q gaps final-minus-adapted and actor-minus-recorded under all three critics; preference switches only where execution actions differ. Same-state stochastic objective differences and gate-gradient components distinguish Q ranking versus latent entropy pressure.
limits: Fit observations can locate learned objective preferences, not realized counterfactual action costs.
Eight samples approximate the positive branch expectation; fixed draws are not a retuned estimator.
Gate partial derivatives do not reproduce total shared-network gradients.
This diagnostic does not select a deployment model, coefficient, threshold or city from the completed evaluation cohort.
code_boundary: Only physical CFCMT-owned frozen runtime; no mutable Thesis reads, imports or writes. Small JSON outputs only.
